semantics.note: Preserves the specified amount, instruments, year, and asserted causal relationship.

contract.note: Reading conversion as the business restructuring is reasonable while separately examining the nonprofit description. Requiring evidence of causation follows the speaker's wording.

evidence.note: Timely company disclosure describes an existing for-profit subsidiary and continued nonprofit control. It qualifies the conversion description but does not establish the charge or its cause.

Timely independent reporting identifies periodic valuation increases as a mechanism. Its roughly $30 billion charge has unspecified attribution scope and is not reconciled to the claimed $41.55 billion combined charge.

reviews.rationale: The nonprofit description is imprecise, and the FT supplies an alternative valuation-based explanation. Neither item establishes or excludes a restructuring-caused $41.55 billion charge on the specified instruments. Without the accounting reconciliation, the causal claim remains unsettled.

attribution.note: Zitron presents the loss reconciliation as his own account of the documents.

semantics.note: Preserves all four amounts and the allocation relationship. The named accounting categories support reading the sentence as attribution of losses.

contract.note: Checking the consolidated loss, attributable loss, and both allocations fairly tests the numerical reconciliation. The context supports distinguishing allocation from actual expense elimination.

reviews.rationale: The packet supplies no independent verification of the complete reconciliation and its two allocation categories. Rounded attributable losses and derivative reporting do not establish all four figures. Arithmetic consistency alone cannot verify the underlying accounts.
